description:
crate-jmap-cid-types/src/digest.rs:73 defines Sha256DigestError as a #[non_exhaustive] struct with a single pub kind: Sha256DigestErrorKind field, and a Display impl that just delegates to self.kind.fmt(f). The wrapper adds zero information over Sha256DigestErrorKind directly.

The intent appears to be the thiserror two-tier pattern (outer struct = stable error type, inner enum = stable matchable variants, outer carries extra context like source location, span, input snippet, backtrace, etc.). That pattern pays off when the wrapper actually carries extra context. Here it does not — the wrapper is just an alias for the kind.

What goes wrong:
- Callers writing match err.kind { ... } when they could match on the enum directly add a level of indirection for no semantic gain.
- #[non_exhaustive] on the wrapper struct prevents callers from constructing Sha256DigestError { kind } literals — a real friction in tests (note digest.rs:378 in the existing test does construct one directly, which works because the test is inside the crate, but external callers cannot). The myoss pass .10 covers the per-variant non_exhaustive question on the *enum*; this finding is about the *wrapper struct*.
- The two-tier shape implies 'future fields coming' that nothing in PLAN.md or the draft suggests are coming.

Two idiomatic resolutions:
(a) Drop the wrapper. Make Sha256DigestErrorKind itself the error type (rename to Sha256DigestError, keep variants). thiserror-style without thiserror. This matches the canonical pattern for crate-internal error enums where no extra context is wanted.
(b) Commit to the wrapper and give it real context fields: input length, a snippet of the offending input, the original &str if its lifetime survives. The myoss .14 / .15 findings (offending byte value, bounded int type) already point at fields that could live on the wrapper if anywhere.

Pre-v0.1.0, either is cheap. Post-publish, both become breaking. Decide now.
title: Sha256DigestError wrapper struct adds no fields over Sha256DigestErrorKind — pick one or commit to context fields
